responsibility: Provides the reusable RTL value-numbering library used by several optimizers to reason about equivalent registers, expressions, and memory references while scanning instructions. It maintains cselib_val objects, hash tables keyed by canonical RTL, register-to-value mappings, memory-address dependency lists, preserved/permanent equivalences, and invalidation logic for sets, calls, autoincrement forms, stack/CFA-related values, and debug locations; passes call its init/lookup/process/finalize APIs rather than reimplement local value tracking. It is a shared upstream equivalence engine for RTL optimizers and schedulers, so invalidation or equivalence mistakes can later appear as scheduling, CSE, combine, or dependency wrong-code symptoms.
same_name_distinction: Implements the cselib library’s behavior and state machinery, whereas gcc/cselib.h only declares the cselib_val/elt structures, flags, and APIs that other RTL passes call. This .cc file contains the actual hash-table lookup, value tracking, invalidation, instruction processing, initialization/finalization, and dump logic behind that interface. Use scheduler files for ready-list/dependency scheduling policy; use cselib.cc for the shared RTL value-equivalence facts those passes may consume.
